title: The taste in water
hook: Krishna answers Arjuna with a list: the best of every kind of thing, and one entry nobody expects
carry: every glory is a spark of God

segments.voice: Yesterday, Arjuna asks: in which forms should I think of you? Your line was the infinite, met through forms. Today, Krishna answers.

Pour a glass of cold water on a hot day and take a long drink. That exact clean taste when you're thirsty. Back in chapter seven, Krishna said: I am the taste in water. Not the water. The taste, the part you can't hold in your hand, that makes water water. Now Arjuna has asked where to look for him, and Krishna answers with a whole list built the same way: the best, the brightest, the deepest of every kind of thing. And somewhere in the middle, one entry that makes people stop and read it twice.
screen: `A LONG DRINK ON A HOT DAY.` → `NOT THE WATER. THE TASTE.` → `A LIST OF THE BEST OF EVERYTHING.`

segments.voice: He begins at the center. Verse twenty: I am the self seated in the heart of all beings, their beginning, their middle and their end. Then the list. Among lights, I am the radiant sun. Among bodies of water, the ocean. Among words, the single syllable Om. Among offerings, the quiet repetition of a sacred name. Among things that stand still, the Himalaya. Among trees, the sacred fig. Among rivers, the Ganga. Among letters, the letter A, the first sound. Among seasons, spring, full of flowers. And, verse thirty-three, I am time that never runs out. Now the surprise. Verse thirty-six: I am the gambling of cheats. Commentators read it more than one way. One reading: Krishna is naming whatever is the most intense of its kind, even the kind no one would choose; whatever grips hardest has a spark of his power in it. Then a wink, verse thirty-seven: among the Pandavas, I am Arjuna, the man he's talking to. Verse forty-one gives the rule for the whole list: whatever is glorious, beautiful, or mighty, know that it springs from a spark of my splendor. And the last verse: but what do you need all this detail for, Arjuna? I hold up this entire universe with a single fragment of myself. This is vibhuti, God's glory showing through the world, and it's why Hindus bathe in the Ganga, circle the sacred fig and begin with Om: each is a spark of the one splendor.
screen: `THE SELF IN THE HEART OF ALL.` · `THE SUN, THE OCEAN, OM, THE GANGA.` · `EVEN THE GAMBLING OF CHEATS.` · `A SPARK OF MY SPLENDOR.` · then, large: `EVERY GLORY, A SPARK OF GOD.`

segments.voice: Take one slow sip of water, or remember the last time you drank when you were really thirsty, and stay with the taste: the cool, the clean, the relief. Then let your attention move to the light, a sound, the air on your skin, and notice what's best in each. If you pray, you can hold verse forty-one in mind: every glory is a spark.
Rasa. Taste, flavor, essence, the part you can't hold in your hand that makes water water. Krishna's handles for the sacred: the best of each kind, every glory a spark of his splendor.
Your line: every glory is a spark of God. A sip of water, the Ganga, the letter A. On to chapter eleven tomorrow.

howItsDone: Many Hindus honor the presences named in Gita chapter ten: they bathe in the Ganga, circle the sacred fig tree, chant Om and repeat a divine name (japa), seeing each as a glimpse of the divine.

original.note: Sanskrit: raso 'ham apsu, 'I am the taste in the waters' (7.8); rasa, taste, flavor, essence.

vibhuti.meaning: God's glory showing through the world

rasa.meaning: taste, flavor, essence: what makes a thing itself

Om.meaning: the sacred single syllable; Krishna's handle among words

Himalaya.meaning: the great mountains; Krishna's handle among things that stand still

Ganga.meaning: the sacred river; Krishna's handle among rivers

Pandavas.meaning: the five brothers, Arjuna among them
